Spec review companion · #108 · snapshot 07b9c78 · 2026-10-21

Give Copilot reviews the whole diff of a large change

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

The change

Copilot reviews see the whole diff

A review of more than 2 changed files gave Copilot one patch file. Copilot's view tool cuts each read at about 40 KB, so a full read depended on Copilot asking again after each cut research.md:14.

Now the diff is inline up to 256 KB whatever the file count, and above that each changed file gets its own patch file plan.md:9.

§1 Inline limit

256 KB stays. The 2-file limit goes. maxInlineFiles stays as an option with no default limit. research.md:25

§2 Per-file patches

Each diff file is split at its diff --git and Submodule lines, so the parts joined are the exact bytes. research.md:39

§3 Prompt list

Each patch is listed with its first line, and Copilot is asked to read every one. research.md:86

§4 The port spec

Spec 005 is not edited, because a merged spec folder is history. research.md:92

§5 Blind plan input files

Files outside the repo are pasted into the prompt file. research.md:101

§6 Release level

Patch, 1.0.18. research.md:107

How it works

Two paths, chosen by size only

Folder life cycle (unchanged)

The folder is made in job storage, removed in finally and on a stop signal. A write that fails partway throws, and Copilot does not start. research.md:59

Examples

Cases that shaped the design

These come from the spec and the tests. The cause test is the only real Copilot run.

PR #106, 11 files, 82 KB

Old: 5 overlapping view reads. New: inline, no tool call, all 11 files read. research.md:10 research.md:17

A renamed file

One patch with both names, because the split keeps git's rename header. spec.md:91

A submodule line with no diff, then a normal file

Two patches. Round 2 of the plan review found that an earlier rule joined them. research.md:52

An empty staged diff

No staged patch file. spec.md:103

1000 changed files

Names get 4 digits and still sort in diff order. research.md:42

Only the review input changes

What to check before approving

Six items

  1. Spec 005 is not updated, though the issue asks for it. The plan follows the constitution instead and records the change here and in the README. research.md:94
  2. Patch, not minor. Both blind plans said minor. The plan says no command, flag or output changes. research.md:108
  3. One file above 256 KB is still one large patch. Copilot must read it in parts. spec.md:89
  4. Untracked text has no total limit. This is the same as on main, and is left as it is. research.md:78
  5. Many small files mean many reads above 256 KB. Accepted, because the issue asks for one patch per file. research.md:68
  6. The cause test is one run each, and Copilot reports itself. The old run's log shows the cuts. The new run made no tool call. research.md:14

The spec defers on purpose: a limit on untracked text, and a split for one very large file.

# Contract: the review input that Copilot gets ## Inline (diff at most 256 KB) The prompt's review input is the context `content`, as today: the commit log, the diff stat and thebranch diff, or the git status, the staged and unstaged diffs and the untracked files. No`--add-dir`. ## Patch folder (diff above 256 KB) The guidance line: > The repository context below is a lightweight summary. Read every patch file listed below with> the view tool before finalizing findings. Each one holds the diff of one changed file. The review input ends with: ```text## Patch Files - <folder>/branch-001.patch: diff --git a/<path> b/<path>- <folder>/branch-002.patch: diff --git a/<old> b/<new>- <folder>/branch-003.patch: Submodule <path> <old>..<new>:``` Each label is the first line of its patch. For the working tree: the `staged-NNN.patch` entries, then `unstaged-NNN.patch`, then`- <folder>/untracked.md: untracked files`. Copilot gets `--add-dir=<folder>`, as today.

# Data Model: Give Copilot reviews the whole diff of a large change ## Review context (`collectReviewContext`) | Field | Change || --- | --- || `inputMode` | `inline-diff` when the diff is at most `maxInlineDiffBytes` (256 KB) and the file count is at most `maxInlineFiles` (default: no limit); otherwise `self-collect` || `collectionGuidance` | `self-collect`: asks Copilot to read every patch file listed below, one per changed file || others | unchanged | ## Patch folder (`jobs/<id>.patches`) | Scope | Files || --- | --- || branch | `branch-001.patch` … one per file or submodule section of the branch diff (research §2) || working tree, gate | `staged-NNN.patch`, `unstaged-NNN.patch` (none for an empty diff), `untracked.md` | - Numbers are padded to at least 3 digits, and to the digits of the patch count when it is more, so  the names sort in diff order.- Joined in order, the patches of one diff are its exact bytes.- The folder is made with mode `0700`, each file with `0600` and `wx`, as today. ## Patch entry (returned by `writeReviewPatches`) | Field | Meaning || --- | --- || `file` | absolute path of the patch file || `label` | the patch's first line (its `diff --git` or `Submodule` line, or the first line of bytes before them), or `untracked files` |

research.md 109 lines
# Research: Give Copilot reviews the whole diff of a large change ## §0 The cause test (2026-10-21) A real Copilot adversarial review of the PR #106 diff (merge `960d3c1` against `829d37f`, 11 files,82 KB, 1507 patch lines) ran with the 1.0.17 plugin, which gives one `branch.patch`. The focus textasked Copilot to list each file as read in full, read in part, or not read. - Copilot said it read every file in full.- Its session log shows 5 `view` calls on `branch.patch`, with the line ranges 1–120, 120–620,  565–1000, 873–1130 and 1130–1507. Each result stopped at about 40 KB (21 to 44 KB of text). After  the 120–620 and 565–1000 calls, Copilot started again before the end it asked for, because the  result was cut there.- So the `view` tool cuts a large read, and a full read depends on Copilot seeing the cut and  asking again. On PR #106 it did not. This time it did. The same review with the new code (the diff inline, same focus text and target) made no tool call.Copilot listed all 11 files as read in full, and named the last line of the last file(`tests/spec-review-page.test.mjs`). Its verdict was `approve`, where the old run raised twofindings (a Principle II wording point and a missing CSP); a model gives different findings ondifferent runs, so the test compares only what was read. ## §1 Inline limit - **Decision**: put the diff inline when it is at most 256 KB, whatever the file count. The  `maxInlineFiles` option stays, with the default "no limit".- **Rationale**: upstream's 2-file limit exists because Codex can run `git diff` itself, one file at  a time. Copilot has no shell in a review, so above the limit it can only `view` a file, which cuts  at about 40 KB (§0). Inline text needs no tool call. The prompt goes to Copilot on stdin, so there  is no command-line limit: `tests/prompt-mode.test.mjs` already checks that a 300 KB prompt reaches  stdin unchanged, and `tests/runtime-hooks.test.mjs` runs the gate with 100 KB on stdin (plan  review round 5 asked for such a test). The 256 KB byte limit stays, as upstream has it.- **Alternatives rejected**: keep the 2-file limit and only split the patch (most tickets would  still need many `view` calls); a higher byte limit (no evidence that it is needed); remove the  `maxInlineFiles` option (upstream has it, and tests use it to force the patch folder). ## §2 Per-file patches above 256 KB - **Decision**: git still writes each diff straight to a file. `writeReviewPatches` then reads that  file as bytes and splits it into `branch-001.patch`, `branch-002.patch` and so on  (`staged-NNN.patch` and `unstaged-NNN.patch` for the working tree), and removes the full file. It  returns each patch with its first line as the label. The number has at least 3 digits, and more  when there are more patches, so the names sort in diff order.- **Split points** (decided 2026-10-21, plan review rounds 1 and 2): a new patch starts at each  line that starts with `diff --git ` or `Submodule `. So a changed submodule gives its  `Submodule <path> a..b:` header as one small patch, then one patch per inner file  (`--submodule=diff` prints the inner files as `diff --git a/<path>/<inner> …`, so each label names  the submodule path). A `Submodule <path> contains modified content` line is its own patch. Bytes  before the first split point go into the first patch, and a non-empty diff with no split point is  one patch, so no byte is lost. Rejected alternatives: split at `diff --git ` lines only, which  leaves a submodule's header at the end of the patch before it and labels it wrongly (round 1);  keep a submodule header with the `diff --git` line after it, which joins an unrelated file to a  header that has no diff of its own (round 2).- **Rationale**: a split of one diff keeps the bytes exact (joined in order, the parts are the full  diff) and keeps renames, binary patches and submodule lines as git prints them. A content line  of a patch starts with a space, `+`, `-` or `\`, and a binary patch line has no space, so no  content line starts with `diff --git ` or `Submodule `. Numbered names keep repo file names out of  the folder's paths, so a name cannot leave the folder or clash.- **Failure**: a write that fails partway (for example a patch file that exists already, since  each file is made with `wx`) throws. `withReviewPatches` already removes the whole folder in its  `finally`, and Copilot does not start. A test covers it.- **Memory** (2026-10-21, plan review round 3): the split reads each diff file whole. A Node  Buffer lives outside the script heap; a file above 2 GB makes the read throw, so the review fails  with that error before Copilot starts, and the folder is removed. Copilot could not read such a  patch today either. The patch list adds one line per file, and the summary already lists every  file name. Rejected alternative: a streaming split in chunks, which adds code for a case that  gives no usable review.- **Patch count** (2026-10-21, plan review round 4): above 256 KB, a change of many small files  needs one `view` call per file, where one large patch needed one call per 40 KB. This is  accepted: the issue asks for one patch per changed file, so that Copilot can see which files it  has not read. Rejected alternative: group small patches into parts of about 40 KB, which brings  back files that hold several changes.- **Alternatives rejected**: one `git diff -- <file>` per file (a rename then shows as an add and a  delete, unless both names are passed; more git calls; quoted names need parsing); file names made  from the repo path (clashes, long paths on Windows, odd characters).- Untracked files keep one `untracked.md`: their text is also in the prompt in both modes, with the  24 KB limit for each file, so a split gives Copilot nothing new.- **Untracked text and the prompt size** (2026-10-21, plan review): the plan review said that  without the file limit, many untracked files make the prompt unbounded. On `main` the untracked  text is in the prompt in both modes already, so the file limit never bounded it; this change adds  at most 256 KB of diff. Not changed here. Rejected alternative: count the untracked bytes toward  the 256 KB limit, which changes behaviour that the issue does not ask about. ## §3 Prompt list - **Decision**: the `## Patch Files` section lists `- <patch path>: <first line of the patch>` (untracked:  `- <path>: untracked files`). The guidance asks Copilot to read every listed file.- **Rationale**: Copilot can see which file each patch holds and which it has not read. ## §4 The port spec - **Decision**: do not edit `specs/005-copilot-plugin-port/`. Record the change here and in the  README section "Differences from the Codex plugin".- **Rationale**: the issue asks for research §2 and the call-site map in spec 005 to be updated, but  spec 005 has merged, and the constitution ("Implementation-to-Spec Consistency") says a merged  spec folder is history that later work does not update. The constitution wins.- **Alternative rejected**: edit spec 005 as the issue asks. ## §5 Blind plan input files - **Decision**: add to the "Blind plan" rule, step 1: when the task uses files outside the repo,  paste their text into the prompt file. The same holds for a plan review prompt file.- **Rationale**: the reviewers' sandbox reads only the repo (#105's blind plan). ## §6 Release level - **Decision**: patch, 1.0.18.- **Rationale**: no command, flag or output changes. Only the review input that Copilot gets  changes ("Is this ticket a release?": a change users do not notice in commands, flags or output).

# Feature Specification: Give Copilot reviews the whole diff of a large change **Feature Branch**: `feature/108-copilot-reviews-whole-diff` **Created**: 2026-10-21 **Status**: Draft **Input**: GitHub issue #108, "Give Copilot reviews the whole diff of a large change". ## Clarifications ### Session 2026-10-21 (plan review) - Q: How does the split treat `--submodule=diff` output? → A: a `Submodule` line also starts a  patch, and the next `diff --git` line starts the next one; bytes before the first header go into  the first patch (research §2).- Q: Does the untracked text need a new limit now that the file limit is gone? → A: no; it is in  the prompt in both modes on `main` already (research §2). ## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)* ### User Story 1 - A review of a usual change sees the whole diff (Priority: P1) A user runs `/copilot:review` or `/copilot:adversarial-review` on a branch or a working tree thatchanges 3 or more files, with a diff of at most 256 KB. Today the plugin gives Copilot one patchfile and Copilot reads only part of it. After this change, the whole diff is in Copilot's prompt. **Why this priority**: most tickets change more than 2 files. Their reviews must see every file. **Independent Test**: review a branch with 3 files and a small diff. The prompt holds the diff ofall 3 files, and Copilot gets no patch folder. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a branch with 3 or more changed files and a diff of at most 256 KB, **When** the user   runs a branch review, **Then** the prompt holds the whole diff and no patch folder is made.2. **Given** a working tree with 3 or more changed files and a staged and unstaged diff of at most   256 KB, **When** the user runs a working-tree review, **Then** the prompt holds the staged and   unstaged diffs. --- ### User Story 2 - A review of a very large change can read each file (Priority: P2) A user reviews a change whose diff is more than 256 KB. The plugin writes one patch per changedfile to its patch folder, and the prompt lists each patch with the changed file that it holds. Eachread is small, and Copilot can see which files it has not read. **Why this priority**: large diffs are rarer, but one large patch file is the case that Copilotread only in part. **Independent Test**: review a change above 256 KB with several files. The patch folder holds onepatch for each file, the patches together are the exact `git diff` bytes, and the prompt liststhem. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a branch diff above 256 KB, **When** the user runs a branch review, **Then** the   folder holds one patch for each changed file, their bytes joined are the exact branch diff, and   the prompt lists each patch with its file.2. **Given** a working-tree diff above 256 KB, **When** the user runs a working-tree review,   **Then** the staged diff and the unstaged diff each give one patch per file, and the untracked   files keep their own file.3. **Given** the stop-time review gate is on and the working-tree diff is above 256 KB, **When**   Claude stops, **Then** the gate gives Copilot the same per-file patches.4. **Given** a review with a patch folder, **When** the review ends, fails or gets a stop signal,   **Then** the folder is removed. --- ### User Story 3 - A blind plan gives both reviewers the input files (Priority: P3) The owner runs the ticket workflow on a task that uses files outside the repo. The "Blind plan" rulesays to paste the text of those files into the prompt file, because the reviewers' sandbox readsonly the repo. **Why this priority**: it affects planning only, and it happens rarely. **Independent Test**: read the "Blind plan" rule in `.claude/skills/workflow-common/REFERENCE.md`. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a task that uses a file outside the repo, **When** the blind plan prompt file is   written, **Then** the rule says to paste that file's text into it. ### Edge Cases - A single changed file whose diff alone is above 256 KB: it gets one large patch. Copilot reads it  in parts with the `view` tool's line range.- A renamed file: its patch holds the rename header and both names, because the patches are split  from the full diff and not made with a file filter.- A binary file: its patch holds git's binary patch text, as today.- A changed submodule: each `Submodule` line is its own patch, and each inner file diff gets its  own patch, labelled with the submodule path. A file diff after a submodule line is never joined  to it. The joined bytes stay exact.- Bytes before the first file or submodule header, or a non-empty diff with no header: they go  into the first patch, so no byte is lost.- A patch file that cannot be written: the review fails before Copilot starts, and the folder is  removed.- A file name with spaces, non-ASCII letters or a quote: the patch file name is a number, so the  name cannot leave the folder or clash. The list shows the name as git prints it in the patch.- The staged or the unstaged diff is empty: it gives no patch files.- Many untracked files: their text is in the prompt in both modes today, with the 24 KB limit for  each file. This does not change. ## Requirements *(mandatory)* ### Functional Requirements - **FR-001**: A review MUST put the whole diff in the prompt when the diff is at most 256 KB,  whatever the number of changed files. This applies to branch scope, working-tree scope and the  stop-time review gate.- **FR-002**: Above 256 KB, the companion MUST write one patch file per changed file, for the branch  diff, and for the staged and the unstaged diff. The patches MUST be split from the exact  `git diff` bytes, so that joined in order they are equal to the full diff.- **FR-003**: The prompt MUST list each patch file with the changed file that it holds, and MUST ask  Copilot to read every listed file.- **FR-004**: The patch folder MUST stay in the plugin's job storage and MUST be removed after the  run and on a stop signal, as today.- **FR-005**: A review MUST NOT give Copilot a shell or `git`.- **FR-006**: The README section "Differences from the Codex plugin" MUST say what differs from  upstream and why.- **FR-007**: The "Blind plan" rule MUST say that the text of input files outside the repo goes into  the prompt file.- **FR-008**: The change MUST raise the plugin version and add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.- **FR-009**: Before the code change, a real Copilot adversarial review of the PR #106 diff MUST run  with the old input (one patch file), and after it with the new input (inline). The PR body MUST  give the files that Copilot says it read each time. ### Key Entities - **Review input**: the prompt text that Copilot gets: either the inline diff, or a summary and the  list of patch files.- **Patch folder**: `jobs/<job id>.patches` in the plugin's job storage, which holds the per-file  patches and `untracked.md`. ## Success Criteria *(mandatory)* ### Measurable Outcomes - **SC-001**: A review of a change of 3 to 11 files and at most 256 KB gives Copilot 100% of the diff  in its prompt.- **SC-002**: Above 256 KB, each patch file starts at a file or submodule header of the diff (the  first one can also hold bytes before it), and the joined bytes are equal to the diff.- **SC-003**: In the PR #106 test, Copilot with the new input says it read every changed file.- **SC-004**: No patch folder is left after a review that ends, fails or is stopped by a signal. ## Assumptions - The 256 KB limit from upstream stays. Copilot's prompt goes on stdin, so the Windows command-line  limit does not apply.- The `maxInlineFiles` option of `collectReviewContext` stays, as upstream has it, but its default  becomes no limit. Tests use it to force the patch folder.- Untracked files keep one `untracked.md` file. Their text is also in the prompt in both modes, so  splitting it gives Copilot nothing new.- The port spec `specs/005-copilot-plugin-port/` has merged, so it is history and is not updated  (constitution, "Implementation-to-Spec Consistency"). --- description: "Tasks for #108: give Copilot reviews the whole diff of a large change"--- # Tasks: Give Copilot reviews the whole diff of a large change **Input**: Design documents from `specs/108-copilot-reviews-whole-diff/` **Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/review-input.md **Tests**: required by the constitution (Principle VI). ## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description` - **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to ## Phase 1: Setup - [x] T001 Run the cause test with the old input (research §0): a Copilot adversarial review of the PR #106 diff with the 1.0.17 plugin, and record which files it read and its `view` calls ## Phase 2: User Story 1 - A review of a usual change sees the whole diff (Priority: P1) **Goal**: a diff of at most 256 KB is inline, whatever the file count (FR-001). **Independent Test**: T003. - [x] T002 [US1] Set `DEFAULT_INLINE_DIFF_MAX_FILES` to no limit in `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs`, and update the file's change notice- [x] T003 [US1] In `tests/git.test.mjs`, change the 3-file test to expect `inline-diff` with all 3 diffs, for the working tree and for a branch; keep the lightweight checks by passing `maxInlineFiles: 0`; a diff of exactly `maxInlineDiffBytes` stays inline and one byte more does not ## Phase 3: User Story 2 - A review of a very large change can read each file (Priority: P2) **Goal**: above 256 KB, one patch per changed file and a list of them (FR-002 to FR-004). **Independent Test**: T005 and T006. - [x] T004 [US2] In `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs`, make `writeReviewPatches` read each diff file as bytes and split it at the split points of research §2 into numbered patches, and return `{ file, label }` entries; change the self-collect guidance (contracts/review-input.md). In `plugins/copilot/scripts/copilot-companion.mjs`, list each entry as `- <file>: <label>` in `withReviewPatches`- [x] T005 [US2] In `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs`, check per-file patches for the working tree and the branch: one per file, joined bytes equal `git diff`, a rename stays one patch, an empty staged diff gives no staged patch, the prompt lists each entry, and the folder is removed- [x] T005b [US2] In `tests/git.test.mjs`, check `writeReviewPatches` directly: a branch with a changed submodule (its `Submodule` line and each inner diff are separate patches) and an ordinary file after it (its own patch), a working tree whose submodule has modified content (its `Submodule` line is its own patch), a binary file, CRLF content and a file with no newline at its end gives joined bytes equal to `git diff`; 1000 changed files give names with 4 digits that sort in diff order; a patch file that exists already makes it throw. In `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs`, a write failure makes the review fail before Copilot starts and removes the folder- [x] T006 [US2] In `tests/runtime-hooks.test.mjs` and `tests/runtime-helpers.mjs`, make the gate's large-diff fixture exceed 256 KB, and check its per-file patches and the folder removal after success, failure and a stop signal- [x] T007 [P] [US2] Update the comment in `plugins/copilot/scripts/stop-review-gate-hook.mjs` and the review flow in `docs/architecture.md` ## Phase 4: User Story 3 - A blind plan gives both reviewers the input files (Priority: P3) - [x] T008 [P] [US3] Add the line for files outside the repo to "Blind plan", step 1, in `.claude/skills/workflow-common/REFERENCE.md` (research §5) ## Phase 5: Polish - [x] T009 Update the README section "Differences from the Codex plugin" (the large-diff and the review gate items)- [x] T010 Run `npm run bump-version -- 1.0.18` and add the `### 1.0.18` entry to `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md`- [x] T011 Run the commands from "Commands" in REFERENCE.md- [x] T012 Run the cause test with the new input (research §0) and put both results in the PR body ## Dependencies - T001 before T002.
